key: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: one full-body pixel-art heavy infantry sprite for a tactical RPG, transparent background. Image 1 is the exact native battle pose and anatomical geometry reference, not a color reference. Image 2 compares the project's Soldier (first), old Heavy Infantry (second, replace this), Bastion Guardian (third), Archer (fourth); use it for style, scale and armor progression. Redesign Heavy Infantry strictly between first and third in armor mass: fuller white plate breastplate, medium single-layer rounded pauldrons, articulated white forearm and shin armor, small blue waist tassets; less bulky than the guardian, more protected than soldier. A steel open-face helmet and flat dark navy short helmet crest/plume, a little solid dark brown hair at temples, no hair highlight. Blue cloth is matte medium muted archer blue, white/ivory plate occupies majority, dark navy contour and necessary restrained cool bluegray shadows. No gold trim, no brown/green tunic, no glossy glints, no extra ornament. Reproduce Image 1 pose precisely: full figure facing LEFT in three-quarter profile, helmet inclines forward, forward arm extends to the left holding the spear, rear arm bent by waist gripping the same spear, long straight brown wooden spear with silver point at LEFT, held almost horizontal across waist with point slightly lower than blunt right butt; BOTH hands grip shaft. No shield in this battle pose (large rounded forms are helmet and shoulder armor). Two armored boots planted, knees slightly bent. Keep realistic compact sprite proportions of the existing game, not oversized chibi head. Whole spear must be fully visible end to end, continuous wooden shaft and silver blunt butt, no floating fragments. Single isolated complete sprite, ample transparent margins, no ground shadow, no text, no UI, no frame, no gradients or antialias halos. Clean carefully stepped pixel-art clusters, limited gentle palette. Deliver only one figure.
battle: Use case: identity-preserve. Production pixel-art sprite sheet on true transparent background. Image 1 is the approved new Heavy Infantry design. Keep EXACTLY this same white plate armor, medium pauldrons, open-face steel helmet, solid dark brown visible hair, flat short navy helmet crest/plume, blue cloth, brown straight spear with pointed steel LEFT end and blunt metal RIGHT butt. Armor stronger than light Soldier but less massive than Bastion Guardian, no giant shield added to battle. Matte cloth and flat hair, no glossy highlights, limited 14-color feel, clean pixel clusters, dark navy outline, warm white primary plate and moderate archer blue. Image 2 is the native POSE reference, NOT a palette or art style reference. Redraw every full figure in matching native posture and body-part arrangement, respecting the weapon and both hands. SIX separate figures in a 3 columns by 2 rows grid, ordered exactly as Image 2. Same figure size in all six cells, fixed helmet/head and chest alignment across phases; animate limbs without whole-body bobbing. Keep complete limbs connected and full spear including rear butt whenever held; no cut-off shafts, no duplicating fingers. Large clear transparent gutters, no overlaps, no labels/text, no grid, no shadows, no UI. The figures must remain crisp and readable as tiny game sprites. Sheet A: ordered native source poses 0,4,5 on first row; 6,7,8 on second row. All face LEFT and hold the spear in the same nearly horizontal waist-level position, point at left slightly lower than right butt. 0 is planted initial guard with both feet apart, 4 settles with slightly staggered boots, 5 lifts and tucks the forward leg diagonally while rear leg supports, 6 transfers weight forward with opposite knee bent, 7 crosses/tucks the legs, 8 extends them into the opposite stride. Closely follow native knees, boot directions, arm bends and spear inclinations shown in Image 2; no invented sword, shield or attack. This is a heavy compact march cycle, not running or lunging.

maps: Use case: identity-preserve. Production small tactical-map pixel-art sprite sheet with TRUE transparent background, no text or panel. Image1 is the same new Heavy Infantry character to adapt to compact map view: open-face steel helmet with solid navy crest, medium white plate chest/pauldrons/gauntlets/greaves, matte blue tunic/tassets, brown wood spear, little solid dark brown hair. No hair or cloth highlights, warm white primary plate, limited gentle blue-white palette and restrained navy outline/shadows; not dull gray. Heavier than Soldier, thinner armor than Bastion Guardian. Image2 is EXACT native anatomical POSE reference, not palette/style. Keep each native-facing direction, feet, elbows, spear angle and shield orientation. In MAP view use one medium rectangular blue shield with white metal border strapped to LEFT FOREARM (unlike the two-handed battle poses). The shield must move WITH its arm, never detached. Connected hands, full arms/legs/boots, no cut pieces, same identical person and armor in all poses. Compact map proportions with readable head about one quarter total body height. Lock helmet/head and chest center in place across a direction pair/idle phases, move limbs only; never shift whole figure or bounce. Do not use breathing/squashing, rescale body or camera between poses. Full spear including rear handle visible whenever not naturally behind the torso. Ample transparent margins and gutters, no effects/shadow, no antialias fringes, no labels. Output THREE full figures in ONE horizontal row, order native0,1,2 from Image2. They all face three-quarter LEFT/front in the same stable armored stance. Shield is on viewer RIGHT and its blue FACE shows as a narrow rectangular surface in exactly the source orientation. Spear is held across the lower chest at shield height, pointed tip to LEFT and complete shaft running through right hand toward the shield; right elbow folded, not a straight flying disconnected arm. Three restrained idle phases match Image2: slightly change spear hand/forearm position against shield and boot knee articulation; the feet/legs follow native frame0,1,2, not large steps. This is a controlled spear-and-shield readying motion with head and torso fixed. No vertical spear here. Keep same helmet, torso size and placement all three.
